column1: # luals parity expectations: one row per corpus case.
#   case          the .lua file in this directory (without extension)
#   luabox        diag | clean — does `luabox check` (strict) report anything?
#   luals         diag | clean — does lua-language-server --check report any
#                 diagnostic from the type-parity code set (see the script)?
#   note          for AGREE rows, what the case pins; for DIVERGE rows
#                 (luabox != luals), WHY the divergence is intentional.
# The two columns are NOT asserted equal — a row where they differ is a
# reviewed, justified divergence, visible in this file rather than buried in
# an allowlist. What the script enforces is that both columns match what is
# written down, so a parity drift in either tool shows up as a diff against
# a claim (the lb0510-matrix discipline, applied to luals parity).
# Measured against lua-language-server 3.13.5 (the version CI pins).
# case
clean_control
column4: control: an annotated, well-typed file is clean in both

column1: trailing_nil_param_omitted
column4: #49: omitting a TRAILING `number|nil` param is fine in both (measured, was guessed before)

column1: optional_param_trailing_omitted
column4: #49: `---@param b? number` omitted — the `?` spelling agrees with the `|nil` spelling

column1: nontrailing_nil_param_omitted
column4: #49 residual RESOLVED BY MEASUREMENT: luals reports missing-parameter for an omitted NON-trailing `number|nil` param, so luabox's conservative trailing-only bound matches luals exactly

column1: string_receiver_methods

column1: string_receiver_misspelt
column4: #48: a misspelt string method is undefined-field there, LB0306 here

column4: baseline: string passed to a number param is rejected by both

column4: baseline: unknown member on a `---@type` instance is rejected by both

column1: duplicate_class_union
column4: #46/#49: two `---@class Config` declarations union their fields in both

column1: duplicate_field_conflict_first_wins
column4: both flag a same-name field re-declared at a different type, by different rules: luals unions (`string|number` fails the number param), luabox keeps the first (LB0311 + LB0300) — divergent semantics, agreeing presence; the semantic divergence is recorded in docs/03-reference/02-limitations.md

column1: renamed_generic_duplicate
column4: INTENTIONAL DIVERGENCE: lua-language-server 3.13.5 does not support generic classes (`---@class Boxed<T>` yields undefined-doc-name for `T`), while luabox implements them per the LuaCATS generics spec — luabox is deliberately ahead, not lagging; re-measure when the pinned luals version gains support
